jobs.description_text: As civilization electrifies, energy demand will continue to outpace the deployment of terrestrial infrastructure required to deliver it. Space solar energy has the potential to decouple energy generation from geography, weather, and traditional transmission constraints, creating an entirely new layer of global energy infrastructure. Overview Energy is building that new layer: satellites that redirect solar energy from geosynchronous orbit to existing terrestrial solar projects using passively safe near-infrared light. Building a system that has never existed requires people who are comfortable working where physics, engineering, manufacturing, and execution meet. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern
jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is designed end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Mechanical Engineering Intern to design the structure that carries our ground beacon system, including transportation of the system from the lab to the field test. The beacon and its system components all have to travel together, set up fast, and stay co-located with our observational telescope. Portable, modular, and rigid are competing goals. You'll own that trade and defend it. Alongside the mounting, you'll characterize what the environment does to the installed system so we know how much of the pointing error budget the structure is spending. This internship supports our program under a Department of War energy investment program. You'll work directly with the optics team to ensure the structure design meets the optical beacon requirements. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design system mounting for three states: pre-delivery, in transit, and installed at the test site - Trade portability and modularity against stiffness and alignment retention, and document the reasoning behind the design you pick - Design a transportable platform to house beacon equipment - Build parametric CAD models and produce drawings a machine shop can quote and manufacture - Analyze environmental effects on the installed system, including temperature and wind loading, and quantify the impact on pointing stability - Characterize transportation effe

jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where the operating concept and every warfighter conversation helps to define how this technology is used. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Deployment Operations Intern to research what rules govern space solar energy operations, and how a warfighter actually operates the system. In support of a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program, you'll research the policy landscape for space and beacon operations and turn it into concrete CONOPS language. You'll research DoW sites for present and future testing, and you'll build the material that makes this technology legible to the people who would use it to feed our broader space solar energy operational guide. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Research U.S. policy and regulation governing space operations and ground-based beacon operations, and translate it into CONOPS language the engineering team can design against - Identify and profile DoW sites for present and future testing, including access, airspace, and environmental considerations - Support warfighter engagement: prepare briefing material, capture feedback in the room, and route it back into CONOPS and design - Draft an operator manual written for the warfighter, not the engineer - Create warfighter and DoW engagement materials that make an unfamiliar technology easy to understand quickly - Track DoW expectations against what we're producing, and flag gaps early WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR FROM YOU - Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program

jobs.title: Optics Intern
jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is aligned, characterized, and field-corrected end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for an Optics Intern to help with the design and building of our ground beacon from the optical bench to a field test site. The beacon is the pointing reference the satellite system will depend on. If it isn't aligned and characterized correctly, nothing downstream works. You'll work hands-on with the emitter and the observational telescope: aligning the laser, characterizing its output, and co-aligning the beacon with the telescope. Then you'll own a problem we haven't solved yet. Once the system is transported to the test site, alignment may shift. You'll design the procedure that brings it back. This internship supports our program under a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program. You'll work alongside our optics and hardware engineers, and your alignment data will feed directly into hardware decisions we make. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Align the beacon laser within its emitter and verify pointing outside the emitter aperture - Characterize laser output - power, beam profile, divergence, and pointing stability - and document the results - Co-align the beacon laser with the observational telescope and verify boresight - Design a repeatable field alignment procedure that corrects misalignment introduced during transport and installation at the DoW site - Write that procedure so a n

jobs.title: Research Engineer - Post-Training
jobs.description_text: Agora gave us a pretrained 8B model. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Build the post-training stack: You build the RL training loop end-to-end: rollout ingestion from the geo-distributed inference pipeline, reward computation, policy updates, and getting updated weights back out to the network. You set the direction, and you make things happen. - Invent the algorithms: Standard RL recipes assume on-policy rollouts from fast, trusted hardware. You adapt them to asynchronous, high-latency, partially trusted generation: staleness tolerance, off-policy corrections, and communication-efficient policy updates. - Ship first post-trained models: You build the evals that show the models are improving, and you take the first decentralized post-trained release from run to public artifact. jobs.title: Research Engineer - Decentralized Training and Inference Verification
jobs.description_text: Our training and inference network is trustless, and the workers are GPUs scattered across the world. Many things can go wrong in this system. An inference worker can return tokens from a cheaper model, or a highly quantized version of the one it's supposed to run. Even with the right model, it can sample with the wrong parameters. Training faces its own attacks, and Agora showed what a permissionless run deals with in practice: participants who disrupt training by dropping updates or flooding the system, free-riders who submit trivial work and collect the rewards, poisoned updates that plant backdoors, attempts to extract private data from gradients and activations, and contributors who inflate their reported work to claim rewards they didn't earn. Sentinel https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03592 is our first published answer on the training side. Your primary role is to come up with efficient algorithms and systems that verify the work: that tokens came from the claimed model and sampling parameters, and that training contributions are what they claim to be. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Own the threat model: You enumerate what a malicious or careless worker can do across pre-training, post-training, and inference — training disruption and denial-of-service, free-riding, model poisoning and backdoors, data extraction from gradients and activations, reputation and reward manipulation — and you keep that model current as the network grows. - Design and calibrate the tests: You build statis

jobs.title: Commercial Counsel/Senior Counsel
jobs.description_text: Perplexity is looking for a commercially minded attorney to join our Legal team. In this role, you’ll own the full commercial legal lifecycle. You will draft, negotiate, and close a wide range of agreements across partnerships, procurement, infrastructure, and licensing. You will build scalable legal infrastructure and enable the business to move quickly without unacceptable risk. You’ll work closely with teams across the business, including product, engineering, security, finance, and sales to close deals, strengthen our data security and compliance posture, and serve as a trusted advisor on the AI-specific legal questions that come with operating at the frontier of this technology. The ideal candidate brings deep experience negotiating a wide range of commercial technology agreements, including infrastructure and compute procurement agreements, a strong command of data privacy and security frameworks, and the practical judgment to make principled risk calls independently. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, knows how to be a true partner to the business without being a bottleneck, and is excited to help build a best-in-class legal function at one of the most consequential AI companies in the world. jobs.title: Internship - Machine Learning Research Engineer
jobs.description_text: Internship Program Berlin Internship program: 12 - 24 weeks, full-time, in-person in the Berlin office. Responsibilities - Relentlessly push search quality forward — through models, data, tools, or any other leverage available. - Train, and optimize large-scale deep learning models using frameworks like PyTorch, leveraging distributed training (e.g., PyTorch Distributed, DeepSpeed, FSDP) and hardware acceleration, with a focus on retrieval and ranking models. - Conduct research in representation learning, including contrastive learning, multilingual, evaluation, and multimodal modeling for search and retrieval. - Build and optimize RAG pipelines for grounding and answer generation. Qualifications - Understanding of search and retrieval systems, including quality evaluation principles and metrics. - Strong proficiency with PyTorch, including experience in distributed training techniques and performance optimization for large models. - Interested in representation learning, including contrastive learning, dense & sparse vector representations, representation fusion, cross-lingual representation alignment, training data optimization and robust evaluation. - Publication record in AI/ML conferences or workshops (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, SIGIR).

This role is hybrid in Belgrade, London or Berlin. Responsibilities - Find and diagnose quality issues in our search pipeline - Design metrics from scratch to track and measure search quality - Build datasets for model training, including LLM-as-a-judge labeling pipelines - Improve search snippet quality and page selection algorithms for indexing - Design and analyze A/B experiments to validate improvements Qualifications - 4+ years of experience as a data analyst or in a related role - Strong coding skills — expected to write production-grade code at a mid-level backend engineer level - Proficiency with SQL and Python - Demonstrated hands-on experience with at least one of the following: - Designing metrics from scratch (not just analyzing existing A/B experiments) - Building labeling pipelines using LLM-as-a-judge - Training ML models that shipped to production with measurable metric improvements - Designing evals with known ground truth (e.g. SimpleQA, BrowseComp) or driving meaningful improvements on such evals Preferred Qualifications - Experience working on search-related products - Knowledge of statistics and A/B experiment design - Experience with Apache Spark or Databricks

The Perplexity API Platform brings our technology to the world's most discerning developers. We believe these same building blocks can and should power the aspirations of builders everywhere. jobs.description_text: We’re looking for a Senior Cinematographer to define how Perplexity looks on film. Working with the Creative Director and Video Lead, you’ll translate our visual identity into a practical cinematographic language, then bring it to life across the team’s day-to-day output. This is a hands-on role. One day you’re shooting a candid office moment or executive interview with a small kit; the next, you’re leading a full camera and lighting crew on a brand film. Most of your time goes to prepping, testing, lighting, and shooting. You’ll also help build and run our in-house studio, from selecting gear and designing flexible lighting setups to keeping the space production-ready. When turnaround is tight, you’ll support media management and light editing. You’ll report to the Video Lead and work closely with the Video Producer, Brand Lead, designers, motion designers, Growth, Comms, Product Marketing, and external production partners. The Producer and Video Lead handle crewing, budgets, schedules, and logistics so you can stay focused on production and craft. However, you should think like a storyteller, not just a technician, bringing your own ideas for how to show our product and people more vividly through moodboards, shot lists, storyboards, and a willingness to experiment. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE The AI Acceleration team’s mission is to make Perplexity the best place to build and ship software with AI agents. We build the infrastructure that engineers and agents rely on, and develop new ways for agents to write, test, review, and ship code. We own the end-to-end development experience at Perplexity, from the environment where code is written to the systems that ship it to production. You’ll work directly with engineers to understand where development slows down, experiment with new approaches, and take promising ideas through to production. This role combines systems engineering, developer experience, and hands-on agent development, with a direct measure of success: helping teams spend less time on delivery overhead and more time building products. This role is deeply cross-functional: you'll partner closely with our Growth and Product Marketing teams to align on positioning, messaging, and funnel strategy, and you care about everything it takes to make a product great: product, interaction, brand, growth, copywriting, engineering, and marketing. jobs.title: Automation Engineer
jobs.description_text: ROLE OVERVIEW With Serval, an automation that used to take a SOW and a quarter now takes a sentence and an afternoon. That one change is why Automation Engineering is becoming the operating model for enterprise services, and why service teams stop being a bottleneck and start being an advantage. As an Automation Engineer, you build Serval's agents directly into the customer's instance, and the tickets stop arriving: onboarding, access requests, approvals, the long tail that clogs a service desk. You'll push Serval past its current limits into new use cases, dogfood unreleased features, bring field ideas back to our product team, and act as a practitioner evangelist for both Serval and Automation Engineering. This is a title we are coining. Nobody has ten years of it yet, so what you build becomes the standard for everyone after you.
